name: security-audit-skill
description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
one_liner: A checklist-driven AI auditor that reads through a codebase, hunts for security bugs in six careful phases, and writes a report that says exactly what it found and how sure it is — instead of one vague AI scan.
buyer: A freelance security consultant or boutique pentest firm that wants to offer faster, cheaper audits without hiring more senior researchers.
business_use_cases: A freelance pentester runs this first on a client's app, triages the confirmed findings, then spends billable hours only on the hard parts.
A seed-stage SaaS startup runs a self-serve audit before a compliance review (SOC 2, enterprise security questionnaire) instead of paying $15k for a quick external pentest.
An open-source maintainer runs it before each major release to catch supply-chain and auth bugs before users report them publicly.

money_ideas.idea: A solo security consultant sells 'AI-assisted audit' packages priced below a traditional pentest, using this to do the first pass.
Offer a subscription 'continuous audit' service for startups that re-runs the skill on every release and emails a diff of new findings.

steal_this: Spin up a one-weekend 'audit-in-a-box' service: clients paste a repo link, get a PDF report generated by this skill within an hour, priced far below a traditional consulting engagement.
